cause.summary: The runner sends a USB-local ClockRequest to Vehicle, but the candidate implements private USB ClockRequest consumption, clock-sync recording, ClockResponse construction and reply service only for Ground.
cause.runner_expectation: Vehicle COM3 SyncOnly: one 28-byte ClockRequest must receive a matching ClockResponse within five seconds.
cause.vehicle_implementation: Vehicle normal local ingress reads Pixhawk UART, not USB Serial RX. Ground-only private-clock functions and USB Serial RX handling are compiled out for Vehicle.
cause.sufficient_explanation: Even if all 28 request bytes reach the MCU USB RX queue, the current Vehicle loop does not consume them, update the sync record, or produce a private ClockResponse.

source_boundaries.fact: Vehicle is assigned SyncOnly while Ground uses the requested run mode.
Both role workflows get a five-second PC acquisition deadline.
The canonical ClockRequest is written to each role's local USB port.
Ground-only conditional begins around all private-clock RX parser/reply state and the handler.
r19_intercept_usb_clock_request exists only inside the Ground conditional.
The sole clock-sync record update is inside that Ground handler, after response construction.
Vehicle collect_local_ingress consumes pixhawk_serial RX, not USB Serial RX.
The separate Ground collect_local_ingress consumes USB Serial RX and invokes the private clock handler at line 5981.
The private ClockResponse/READY service block is explicitly runtime-diagnostic Ground only.
The loop's failed-runtime USB request collection and private service are also Ground-only.
The PC workflow rejects an unanswered request as PcAcquisitionDeadlineExpired.

offline_reproduction.method: Compile the exact sealed staged bridge per role against existing host fakes and the existing vc_lora_core library; inject the current live request into modeled MCU USB RX; run the actual loop_bridge for 600 loops and 6000 ms.

separated_or_rejected_explanations: A delayed PC reader is not needed to explain this failure: the reader had started 1242.11 ms before the PC write, while the missing Vehicle request handler remains sufficient even under perfect modeled delivery.
A malformed request is not needed: the exact captured request passes the core CRC parser and private nonce codec, and Ground responds to the same bytes in the positive control.
The failure cannot yet be called ClockResponse USB IN loss: no Vehicle ClockResponse is constructed by the current firmware path.
Clock-sync count zero is not standalone proof that USB OUT hardware lost the request, because Vehicle never consumes the USB RX queue.
The generic diagnostic FlushFailed/retry history is a separate USB TX issue; a working/recovered diagnostic TX path does not implement USB RX clock handling.
next_design_decision_not_implemented: Either declare Vehicle USB capture TX-only and do not request a clock exchange, or implement a diagnostic-only Vehicle clock-request consumer and exclusive bounded reply path, then verify it test-first. Ground private ARM must remain Ground-only and no private clock/diagnostic bytes may leak to Pixhawk or E220.
limitations: The host model assumes that bytes have already reached the MCU RX queue; it does not prove that the physical live USB OUT transaction delivered them.

AUX ISR/readiness observation instrumentation is disabled only in the host reproduction because the existing host fakes have no GPIO ISR backend. Ground-only handler preprocessing and the actual bridge logic remain unchanged.
The reproduction establishes a sufficient software integration cause, not the absence of additional USB driver or hardware faults.
No product throughput, RF delivery, 932-parameter completeness, acceptance, or Deployment claim follows from this diagnosis.
